storm.title: SUPER TYPHOON
storm.name: CHAMPI
storm.names: Philippines: Rosal · Taiwan: 薔琵 · Japan: 台風30号 チャンパー

show_open.label: Show open
show_open.content: A short cold open introducing the broadcast as a continuously updating watch on Super Typhoon Champi (Rosal) in the Western Pacific. Sets expectations that the information refreshes throughout the stream.

storm_position.label: Current storm position
storm_position.content: The current position, intensity (sustained winds, gusts, central pressure), movement direction and speed of Super Typhoon Champi (Philippine name Rosal, JTWC 29W, JMA typhoon 2630) in the Western Pacific, as reported by the official warning agencies JMA, JTWC and PAGASA, with the time of each analysis.

track_forecast.label: Track and intensity forecast
track_forecast.content: The projected track and intensity forecast for Super Typhoon Champi (Rosal) over the next 72 hours: forecast positions and times, expected intensity changes, the forecast uncertainty, and any disagreement between JMA, JTWC and PAGASA, including when it enters the Philippine Area of Responsibility and nears Taiwan and the Sakishima islands.

local_impacts.label: Expected local impacts
local_impacts.content: Expected on-the-ground impacts of Super Typhoon Champi (Rosal) for populated areas in its path in the northern Philippines (Batanes, Babuyan Islands, Northern Luzon, Bicol), Taiwan (Yilan, Hualien, the north) and Japan's Sakishima and Okinawa islands: rainfall totals, storm surge and seas, wind damage potential, tropical cyclone wind signals, evacuation orders, and school, work or transport suspensions, each attributed to the issuing agency.

show_close.label: Show close
show_close.content: A brief sign-off reminding viewers that the broadcast loops with refreshed data on Typhoon Champi and pointing them to PAGASA, CWA and JMA for evacuation decisions.

anchor_neutral.label: Neutral news anchor
anchor_neutral.content: You are writing copy to be read aloud by a single news anchor. Write in plain spoken English, in complete sentences, with no headings, bullet points, stage directions, or markdown. Lead with the most recent and most decision-relevant fact. Attribute every claim to its source agency by name. Never invent numbers, timestamps, or place names that are not present in the supplied source material; if a figure is missing, say that it has not been reported. Target roughly 220 to 260 seconds (about 4 minutes) of spoken delivery. Use the time to cover every reported detail and explain how the pieces fit together, not to repeat yourself.

anchor_urgent.label: Urgent safety bulletin
anchor_urgent.content: You are writing an urgent public-safety bulletin to be read aloud by a single anchor. Write in plain spoken English with short, direct sentences. Lead with the specific action the audience should take and the areas affected. Attribute every instruction to the issuing authority. Never invent an evacuation order, a shelter location, or a casualty figure that is not present in the supplied source material. Do not speculate beyond what the sources state. Target roughly 220 to 260 seconds (about 4 minutes) of spoken delivery. Use the time to cover every reported detail and explain how the pieces fit together, not to repeat yourself.

station_ident.label: Station identification
station_ident.content: You are writing a short station identification to be read aloud by a single anchor. Write two to three sentences of plain spoken English. Do not cite specific figures or forecasts. Target roughly 15 to 20 seconds of spoken delivery.
